claims.text: The FOMC raised the target range for the federal funds rate to 4-1/2 to 4-3/4 percent.

citations.quotation: the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 4-1/2 to 4-3/4 percent.

claims.text: The Board of Governors voted unanimously to raise the interest rate paid on reserve balances to 4.65 percent, effective February 2, 2023.

citations.quotation: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to raise the interest rate paid on reserve balances to 4.65 percent, effective February 2, 2023.

claims.text: The two rates are distinct: the federal funds rate target range is a policy target corridor (4-1/2 to 4-3/4 percent), while the interest on reserve balances is a specific administered rate (4.65 percent) used to help keep the effective federal funds rate within that range.

citations.quotation: the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 4-1/2 to 4-3/4 percent.
raise the interest rate paid on reserve balances to 4.65 percent, effective February 2, 2023.

counterarguments.text: One might conflate the reserve balance rate (4.65 percent) with the upper bound of the target range (4-3/4 percent) or the primary credit rate (4.75 percent); the sources show they are separate decisions — the IORB is set by the Board of Governors at 4.65 percent, while the discount (primary credit) rate was separately raised to 4.75 percent.

citations.quotation: voted unanimously to approve a 1/4 percentage point increase in the primary credit rate to 4.75 percent, effective February 2, 2023.

limitations: Sources are partial excerpts of the February 1, 2023 statement and implementation note; the full documents are not provided.
